title: Void Functions
concept: Functions that don't return a value use the Unit return type — they perform actions like printing or modifying state.
why: Not every function needs to compute a result. Some just do things — print messages, update data, or trigger actions.
tips: You can omit `-> Unit` — it's the default
`()` is the only value of type Unit
Void functions are all about SIDE EFFECTS — things they do to the world
common_mistakes: Trying to assign a void function's result to a variable: `let x = say_hello();`
Writing `return;` in a void function — just let it end naturally
Forgetting that void functions can still take parameters
